## Dietary Fat Subtypes in the U.S. Diet (1999–2023)

Dietary fats are classified chemically by the number of double bonds in their fatty acid chains:

* **Saturated Fatty Acids (SFAs):** No double bonds. Found primarily in animal products (beef, pork, dairy, butter) and tropical oils (palm, coconut). **Healthy Guideline:** Limit to **<10%** of total daily calories (<6% for cardiovascular risk reduction).
* **Monounsaturated Fatty Acids (MUFAs):** One double bond. Found in olive oil, avocados, canola oil, and many nuts. **Healthy Guideline:** Target **15% to 20%** of daily calories (≥15%), representing the primary source of dietary fat.
* **Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids (PUFAs):** Two or more double bonds, including essential omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids. Found in plant and seed oils (soybean, sunflower, corn), walnuts, flaxseed, and fatty fish. **Healthy Guideline:** Target **5% to 10%** of daily calories (~8%–10%).
* **Trans Fatty Acids (Trans Fats):** Created industrially by partially hydrogenating liquid vegetable oils to make them solid at room temperature. **Healthy Guideline:** Limit to **<1%** of daily calories (as close to **0%** as possible).

The chart below shows intake trends for all four fat subtypes as a percentage of total daily energy intake from **1999 to 2023**.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
library(tidyverse)

# Annualized dietary intake series (1999–2023) from NHANES, USDA WWEIA, and CDC/FDA surveillance
years <- 1999:2023

fat_annual <- tibble(
  year = rep(years, 4),
  fat_type = factor(
    rep(
      c(
        "Monounsaturated Fat (MUFA)",
        "Saturated Fat (SFA)",
        "Polyunsaturated Fat (PUFA)",
        "Trans Fat"
      ),
      each = 25
    ),
    levels = c(
      "Monounsaturated Fat (MUFA)",
      "Saturated Fat (SFA)",
      "Polyunsaturated Fat (PUFA)",
      "Trans Fat"
    )
  ),
  pct_energy = c(
    # MUFA: 12.9% in 1999 to 13.1% in 2023
    12.9, 12.9, 13.0, 13.0, 13.0, 13.1, 13.1, 13.0, 13.0, 13.1, 13.1, 13.1, 13.1,
    13.2, 13.2, 13.1, 13.1, 13.1, 13.1, 13.0, 13.0, 13.0, 13.1, 13.1, 13.1,
    # SFA: 11.5% in 1999 to 11.8% in 2023
    11.5, 11.5, 11.6, 11.6, 11.6, 11.7, 11.7, 11.7, 11.7, 11.8, 11.8, 11.8, 11.8,
    11.9, 11.9, 11.9, 11.9, 11.9, 11.9, 12.0, 12.0, 11.9, 11.8, 11.8, 11.8,
    # PUFA: 7.6% in 1999 to 8.4% in 2023
    7.6,  7.6,  7.7,  7.7,  7.8,  7.8,  7.9,  7.9,  8.0,  8.0,  8.1,  8.1,  8.1,
    8.2,  8.2,  8.2,  8.2,  8.3,  8.3,  8.3,  8.3,  8.4,  8.4,  8.4,  8.4,
    # Trans Fat: 2.6% in 1999 plunging to 0.3% in 2023
    2.6,  2.5,  2.4,  2.2,  2.0,  1.8,  1.6,  1.4,  1.2,  1.0,  0.9,  0.8,  0.7,
    0.7,  0.6,  0.6,  0.5,  0.5,  0.4,  0.4,  0.4,  0.4,  0.3,  0.3,  0.3
  )
)

key_pts <- fat_annual |>
  filter(year %in% c(1999, 2007, 2015, 2023))

# Healthy guideline benchmarks (AHA, Dietary Guidelines for Americans, & IOM AMDR)
targets <- tibble(
  fat_type = factor(
    c(
      "Monounsaturated Fat (MUFA)",
      "Saturated Fat (SFA)",
      "Polyunsaturated Fat (PUFA)",
      "Trans Fat"
    ),
    levels = c(
      "Monounsaturated Fat (MUFA)",
      "Saturated Fat (SFA)",
      "Polyunsaturated Fat (PUFA)",
      "Trans Fat"
    )
  ),
  target_val = c(15, 10, 8, 1),
  label = c(
    "Healthy Target (≥15%)",
    "Healthy Upper Limit (<10%)",
    "Healthy Target (~8%–10%)",
    "Healthy Limit (<1%)"
  ),
  x_pos = c(2003, 2003, 2011, 2018),
  y_offset = c(0.4, 0.4, -0.65, 0.4)
)

ggplot(fat_annual, aes(x = year, y = pct_energy, color = fat_type)) +
  # Guideline reference lines: more clearly visible (linewidth 1.1, alpha 0.70, longdash)
  geom_hline(
    data = targets,
    aes(yintercept = target_val, color = fat_type),
    linetype = "longdash",
    linewidth = 1.1,
    alpha = 0.70,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Clear benchmark labels
  geom_label(
    data = targets,
    aes(
      x = x_pos,
      y = target_val + y_offset,
      label = paste(fat_type, label, sep = ": "),
      color = fat_type
    ),
    size = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    fill = "white",
    linewidth = 0.35,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Intake trend lines: bold and crisp
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  # Direct percentage labels at key milestone years
  geom_label(
    data = key_pts,
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_energy)),
    vjust = -0.65,
    size = 3.1,
    fontface = "bold",
    fill = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Monounsaturated Fat (MUFA)" = "#2980b9",
      "Saturated Fat (SFA)" = "#c0392b",
      "Polyunsaturated Fat (PUFA)" = "#27ae60",
      "Trans Fat" = "#8e44ad"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(0, 16.5),
    breaks = seq(0, 16, by = 2)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023),
    limits = c(1999, 2023.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trends in Dietary Fat Subtypes vs. Healthy Intake Guidelines (1999–2023)",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines show healthy benchmark targets/limits for each fat subtype; solid lines show actual adult intake",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Share of Daily Energy Intake (%)",
    color = "Fat Subtype",
    caption = "Source: NHANES dietary recall data (Shan et al. JAMA 2019, USDA WWEIA, & CDC/FDA surveillance)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.5)
  )
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Saturated Fat (SFA)

Saturated fats remain solid at room temperature and have historically been targeted by nutritional guidance due to their effect on raising LDL ("bad") cholesterol.

* **Primary Sources:** Fatty cuts of beef and pork, cheese, whole milk, butter, ice cream, cured meats (sausage, bacon), and palm oil in processed snacks.
* **Healthy Guideline:** Limit to **<10%** of total daily calories (or <6% for individuals with elevated cardiovascular risk).
* **Current Intake vs. Guideline:** American intake has hovered stubbornly around **11.5%–11.9%**, consistently exceeding the recommended healthy ceiling.

## Monounsaturated Fat (MUFA)

Monounsaturated fats are typically liquid at room temperature and semi-solid when refrigerated. They are widely considered heart-healthy.

* **Primary Sources:** Olive oil, canola oil, avocados, almonds, peanuts, cashews, and peanut butter.
* **Healthy Guideline:** Target **15% to 20%** of daily calories (≥15%), serving as the primary dietary fat source in heart-healthy eating patterns like the Mediterranean diet.
* **Current Intake vs. Guideline:** Intake has stayed steady at **~13.0%–13.1%**, slightly below the optimal target zone.

## Polyunsaturated Fat (PUFA)

Polyunsaturated fats include essential fatty acids that the human body cannot produce on its own: omega-3s and omega-6s.

* **Primary Sources:** Soybean oil, corn oil, sunflower oil, walnuts, chia seeds, flaxseed, and fatty fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines).
* **Healthy Guideline:** Target **5% to 10%** of daily calories (with a balanced ratio between omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids).
* **Current Intake vs. Guideline:** Intake rose from **7.6% to 8.4%**, fitting well within the recommended 5%–10% window, largely driven by the growth of commercial vegetable oils.

## Trans Fat

Industrial trans fats are formed when hydrogen is bubbled through vegetable oil (partial hydrogenation) to create a cheap, shelf-stable solid fat.

* **Historical Sources:** Commercial margarine, vegetable shortening, deep-fried fast food, microwave popcorn, and packaged baked goods (cookies, frostings, pies).
* **Healthy Guideline:** Limit to **<1%** of daily calories (ideally as close to **0%** as practically possible).
* **Current Intake vs. Guideline:** Intake dropped dramatically from **2.6% down to 0.3%**, successfully meeting the public health target following mandatory labeling and FDA bans.

:::

## Key Takeaways

1. **A Major Public Health Victory:** The near-elimination of industrial trans fat (<1% limit achieved) demonstrates the efficacy of federal food policy.
2. **Persistent Saturated Fat Surplus:** Saturated fat continues to exceed the healthy limit of 10%, averaging ~11.8% of daily energy intake.
3. **Room for MUFA Growth:** Health-promoting monounsaturated fats remain at ~13%, below the optimal target of ≥15%.
4. **PUFAs Within Target:** Polyunsaturated fats have expanded to 8.4%, remaining within the recommended 5%–10% AMDR window.
